transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Harini (CTO, Northforge), Ethan (Eng Lead), Priya (Security), Liam (PM)

Summary:
Northforge is evaluating Redwood for a phased pilot: start with PLG/self-serve API credits to get to first token, then a short Dedicated pilot for predictable throughput and strict data controls. Main constraints: PII in prompts, EU data residency for some customers, sub-100ms tail latency for a low-latency inference path, and an internal mandate to prefer managed services unless security review requires Private (VPC/on-prem).

Topics covered:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) and free credits/quickstart flow
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, data residency)
- Security: SOC2, SAML/SSO, audit logs, KMS/HSM integration
- Benchmark plan and pilot success criteria
- Next steps and owners

Action items (captured in notes above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I see Harini, Ethan, Priya, Liam, and Diego is here on our side. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE, and Diego is our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Harini: Hey thanks, we only have about 45-ish minutes, so we'll try to keep it tight. Quick context: Northforge is building an assistant and an inline code-search feature. We're trying to figure out how to get to first token quickly with minimal ops, but also keep an option for a private deployment if the security review requires it later.
[00:35] Diego: Great, that matches a lot of folks we talk to — two-stage path makes sense: start PLG/self-serve to validate product signals, then shift sensitive traffic to Dedicated or Private.
[00:48] Ethan: Our main non-negotiable is latency — some user flows need <100ms p95. Cost is important but secondary for initial pilot. Also, we have EU customers; data residency is a must for that subset.
[01:06] Priya: From security side, must have SOC2, SSO via SAML or OIDC, audit logs, and support for a customer-managed KMS. Also want to understand token retention and model cache behavior.
[01:23] Maya: Totally — quick answers up front: Redwood Hosted supports quickstart with free credits to get to first token in minutes, our Console shows per-route latency and token costs. Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and optional VPC peering. Private (on-prem) is available for regulated workloads but has longer lead times. We'll share a security pack after this call.
[01:48] Liam: Quick question — what does the quickstart actually look like? Can a single engineer get a test running without infra?
[01:56] Diego: Yes, the PLG flow is deliberately small. You sign up, you get credits, we provide an SDK and a curl example. In practice engineers are hitting their first token in under an hour for basic prompts. We'll send the quickstart guide — it's the usual curl + Python SDK snippet plus sample prompt sets.
[02:14] Ethan: When you say "credits", are there constraints on which models or regions we can test? We need EU region testing specifically.
[02:23] Maya: Credits are usable for most hosted models; we'll note region constraints in the credit terms. We have hosted endpoints in eu-west and some other regions — we can validate availability for the specific model you want.
[02:34] Harini: Okay. On the Dedicated path, curious about autoscaling and burst behavior — we might have spiky traffic. How does Redwood handle bursts without overprovisioning?
[02:44] Diego: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and a burst pool. The idea is you reserve baseline capacity and allow short bursts to be served by the burst capacity. There's also routing policies to fallback to cheap model variants if capacity is constrained.
[03:01] Ethan: Sounds useful. How does routing impact latency? Does fallback to lower-cost models increase tail latency due to model load times?
[03:11] Diego: Good Q — we use warm pools and KV/prefix caching to avoid cold-start penalties. If a fallback model is architecture-compatible, we can route without incurring the full cold start. But of course, larger model switches can affect latency.
[03:28] Priya: About data retention — we cannot have customer prompts retained by a third party. What are Redwood's retention and deletion guarantees for Hosted?
[03:37] Maya: Hosted, by default, does not use data for training; we support contract terms for no-retention. For Dedicated and Private, customers have stronger isolation. We'll include the exact legal language in the security pack.
[03:50] Harini: Do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) — HSM/KMS integration?
[03:55] Diego: Yes, Dedicated supports BYOK with integrations to major KMS providers and an option for HSM. Private allows full customer-managed keys on-prem.
[04:06] Liam: Can you run a short benchmark for our 1k-token prompts — we need throughput and p95 numbers. What's the easiest way to get consistent numbers?
[04:14] Diego: We'll share a small benchmark harness. Usually the easiest is our sample script that sends batched requests at realistic concurrency. We'll include instructions to capture p50/p95 and token costs.
[04:28] Ethan: For the pilot, we'd like the benchmark to reflect our prompt complexity — there's code snippets, tables, etc. Is there a quantization or model guidance for cost/latency tradeoffs?
[04:38] Diego: Absolutely — Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles and model variants by workload. For code-heavy prompts, architecture choices matter; we'll recommend a mid-size model with optimized kernels — that tends to be the best latency/cost balance.
[04:54] Harini: Any gotchas with KV cache? We use mult-turn contexts; cache eviction could matter with a long context.
[05:01] Diego: Cache sizes and eviction policies are tunable. We can configure longer KV retention for Dedicated, and Private gives you full control. There's also prefix caching which can reduce token compute significantly for repeated starts.
[05:13] [crosstalk] Maya: --- and we can show the Console metrics...
[05:18] Harini: Sorry missed that, go ahead.
[05:20] Maya: No worries. The Console provides per-route latency breakdowns, token costs, and tracing hooks. That'll help you decide which calls need Dedicated vs Hosted.
[05:32] Priya: We need audit logs for every request and SSO for team access. Does Redwood log token-level events and provide an immutable audit trail?
[05:41] Diego: Yes — audit logs, per-request metadata, and RBAC are part of our enterprise features. Logs can be shipped to your SIEM via S3 or direct integrations.
[05:52] Harini: How long to spin up Dedicated? We're a small team and don't want long procurement or infra time.
[05:58] Maya: Dedicated typically takes 2-4 weeks for baseline capacity provisioning post-contract. Private/on-prem is longer — depending on network/security reviews maybe 6-12 weeks. For rapid testing you can start with Hosted credits immediately.
[06:09] Liam: If we start with Hosted for TTFT, then move to Dedicated, how seamless is the model/versioning and rollout?
[06:17] Diego: The API and config layer are consistent across modes. You can pin model versions and do canary rollouts. The smart routing layer helps with fallback during rollouts.
[06:27] Ethan: Any experience with cost surprises on PLG tests? We want to avoid accidental cost spikes if a test goes rogue.
[06:35] Maya: You can set hard quotas, per-route caps, and alerting. The Console also shows token-level spend in near real-time. For PLG we'll recommend conservative quotas and automated alerts.
[06:48] Harini: Competitors question — we briefly looked at Anthropic and a small internal infra approach. What would you say is Redwood's differentiation?
[06:58] Maya: Two things: production-first tooling for observability/rollouts and flexible deployment paths (hosted-to-dedicated-to-private) with predictable economics. Also, the Optimize tooling helps keep unit cost down with actionable suggestions.
[07:15] Priya: Legal/procurement question — do you support standard enterprise clauses for data residency and liability?
[07:22] Maya: Yes, we have an enterprise contract template and specific add-ons for compliance. We'll surface the legal package after this call.
[07:30] Harini: Alright let's define success criteria for the pilot — for us it's: (1) TTFT: engineer can demo in <1 day; (2) Benchmark: p95 <100ms for specified path in Dedicated pilot; (3) Security signoff: SOC2 + BYOK or Private if needed.
[07:48] Ethan: Agree on those. Also want to ensure the bench harness captures real concurrency patterns.
[07:55] Diego: We'll craft the harness to mirror your traffic pattern — send it as part of the next step.
[08:02] Liam: Timeline — we'd like to get a proof-of-concept running in 2 weeks and Dedicated pilot in ~4 weeks. Is that realistic?
[08:10] Maya: Starting with Hosted credits, POC in 1-2 weeks is realistic. Dedicated in 4-6 weeks depending on contract speed.
[08:18] [00:08:18] Harini: Ok final questions: does Redwood support on-prem private air-gapped for regulated customers?
[08:25] Diego: Yes, that's our Private deployment option — it requires more lead time and network validation.
[08:31] Harini: And monitoring/data egress — if we use Dedicated in eu-west, will logs ever cross regions?
[08:38] Maya: No, we can configure logging and storage to remain in-region for EU Dedicated. We'll document that in the security pack.
[08:46] Priya: Please include a red-team checklist and a copy of your SOC2 report.
[08:51] Maya: Will do. We'll attach SOC2 and the compliance packet in the follow-up email.
[09:00] Ethan: One more small detail — do you do model explainability or lineage for audit purposes?
[09:07] Diego: We include request/response hashes and model version metadata in audit logs; for deeper explainability we recommend instrumenting prompts and outputs in your eval pipeline.
[09:18] Harini: That should work.
[09:20] Maya: Great — recap of next steps: I'll send Dedicated pricing, security pack, and a quickstart guide with credits. Diego will send the benchmark script and example SDK snippets. Harini to confirm pilot scope and KMS needs. We'll schedule a technical deep dive between Diego and Ethan next week.
[09:40] Liam: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:43] Harini: Thanks, bye.
